verdict.why: Both cover the brief's four asks (role/route review, meanings/text split, per-call spend ledger with day/month summary and USD 5,000 warning, quality), and both fix the two measured defects (BYOK cost hidden in usage.cost_details.upstream_inference_cost; --judge-only zeroing the panel's cost). Option X wins on criterion 1 and 2. (a) Tracking: the order says every token call is written down; X books one ledger row for every request, including failed and timed-out calls (Design 5, C5, REQ-8), while Y books only attempts that returned usage (D17, R5) — a request the provider billed but answered without usage would leave no row, weakening the accounting. (b) 'One request each': X's REQ-4 is an absolute no-retry, matching the owner's words; Y's D9 allows one retry when no usage came back, which is a second request and contradicts the order as relayed, however reasoned the exception. (c) The owner's order exempts no spec size from the thinker; X applies the split to every size when in force (Q5, 'the order has no size exemption'), Y invents an S exemption (D2) — a defensible decision but a weaker reading of the brief. (d) Cost rule: X branches on the measured is_byok/upstream evidence (rule 1–3) and prices-with-fallback; Y's D15 ('u present and c < u gives c + u') can double-count whenever a non-BYOK call returns both fields with c < u — a real edge X names in its cost_source scheme. (e) Contracts: X's C1–C7 give a zero-context implementer exact schemas, exit codes, grep-verifiable invariants (urlopen only in spend.py), and a degraded path (meanings --from-file --reason) for thinker-route outage, which Y handles by stopping the spec and asking the owner — pushing a tactical question up. Y is genuinely strong: its replay test with refutation conditions (D28, Risks) is the better answer to 'do not lose quality' on criterion 2, its R8 round/global ledger reconciliation is a check X lacks, and its per-purpose call refusal (C4) is a neat guard against repeat paid calls. But X's canary with baseline comparison (Rollout step 6) also satisfies the quality ask verifiably, and X is tighter on the order's exact words where the two diverge.
risks: X is long for an M spec; the word ratchet forces dense doctrine edits that an implementer must execute carefully, and its summary/ceiling surface (C7) plus estate cache logic adds build weight beyond the brief's minimum

X's degraded path lets subscription-session meanings stand in for the paid thinker without naming that the session runs the thinker's model; Y's D24 is more explicit that only the same model on another route may substitute
X's --judge-only twice keeps both judge rows in the round total, so a rerun habit could quietly double the round's recorded judge spend; Y refuses a second verdict once one is parsable

X's estate figure takes max(Observatory, local), assuming the provider figure contains this host's calls; if Observatory's totalUsd is per-project rather than estate-wide the warning could understate — both options share the unverified-JSON-shape risk (X Q7, Y Risks)
